scorecard.rationale: In a five-person Parkinson and Lewy body dementia aroma series, two improved on swallowing tests, one was unchanged and two dropped out. Other aroma series gave mixed results. Topical piperine in burning-mouth syndrome reported binary dysphagia with different baseline and follow-up denominators. Swallowing severity after eating cracked pepper remains open. The full Rofes original distinguishes a favorable acute instrumental high-concentration PAS comparison (3.25 to 1.85, p=.003) from an inconclusive low-concentration comparison (2.10 to 1.95, p=.521). All four neurodegenerative participants were in the lower group and diagnosis-specific results were not supplied. The study fixes the unfortified nectar first for everyone. The edible-film experiment measures detection and adaptation, without linking cracked pepper particle texture, local dose or timing to airway protection. Alongside mixed aroma series, the different preparations and absent comparable solid-food result leave the culinary sign open. The full black pepper oil trial randomized 35 participants per group and showed shorter swallowing-reflex latency after nasal inhalation than lavender or water in older post-stroke residents. The later meta-analysis pools different TRP agents and the excluded crossover is the distinct pharyngeal menthol study. Lee reports bulk piperine concentrations in peppers and other foods but does not measure delivery during consumption. The strongest relevant oral piperine comparison and inhalation studies remain too different in preparation, setting, or endpoint to assign a sign for eating cracked pepper in Parkinson disease.
